description: Issue #1011: swaps BaseImportVM<T,P>.SetTemplateData's fp.GetFileTenantScoped(...) call (BaseImportVM.cs, ~line 326) back to the flag-driven fp.GetFile(...) overload -- a compile-preserving method-name swap (both overloads exist on WtmFileProvider; GetFile is not obsolete, so this mutant does not even change build warnings). Checked against WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.VM.BaseImportVMTenantScopedReadTests1011.SetTemplateData_EnforceTenantFileScopeFalse_CrossTenantUploadFileId_Blocked, which seeds a cross-tenant FileAttachment (tenant B) whose content is a workbook MediumFixWorkbookBuilder.BuildWithBlankRows produces -- already proven elsewhere (ImportMediumFixTests, via BytesInjectedImportVM, which reproduces the same row-parsing control flow) to parse cleanly into exactly one TemplateData row with zero validation errors -- sets EnforceTenantFileScope=false, and calls the REAL, non-overridden SetTemplateData() as tenant A's caller through a WTMContext whose CreateDC is wired to return that tenant-A-scoped IDataContext directly (SingleConnectionImportWtmContext, same bypass pattern as FrameworkControllerFileAccessTest.SingleConnectionFileAccessWtmContext -- Wtm.CreateDC('default') cannot be mocked, per .claude/rules/testing.md). Under the fix, GetFileTenantScoped keeps the ITenant query filter ON unconditionally regardless of the flag, so the cross-tenant file does not resolve: TemplateData stays empty and ErrorListVM gets exactly the 'WrongTemplate' entry. Under this mutant, GetFile with EnforceTenantFileScope=false calls IgnoreQueryFilters() -- no tenant predicate at all -- so the cross-tenant file DOES resolve, the workbook parses successfully, and TemplateData ends up with 1 row / 0 errors instead: the test's Assert.AreEqual(0, TemplateData.Count) fails with Actual:<1>, proving the test genuinely depends on which overload SetTemplateData calls, not on an incidental side effect.
target_symbol: BaseImportVM<T, P>.SetTemplateData() -- the fp.GetFileTenantScoped(...) call, line ~326

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.VM.BaseImportV: a cross-tenant UploadFileId must not be parsed into any template rows

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first) with the mutant patch applied: "Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<0>. Actual:<1>. #1011: a cross-tenant UploadFileId must not be parsed into any template rows — got 1. Errors: "
green_test_decoupling: Per .claude/rules/testing.md's binding rule ('a mutant's positive control must not touch the mutated decision path'), traced separately for each green test: (1) WtmFileProviderTenantScopedReadTests1011.GetFileTenantScoped_EnforceTenantFileScopeFalse_SameTenantGuid_ReturnsFile calls WtmFileProvider.GetFileTenantScoped directly -- BaseImportVM.SetTemplateData (the only method this patch touches) is never on its call path at all, so the mutated line cannot execute for this test; this is the 'call graph never reaches the mutated line' shape. (2) BaseImportVMTenantScopedReadTests1011.SetTemplateData_EnforceTenantFileScopeFalse_SameTenantUploadFileId_Succeeds DOES reach the mutated line (it also drives the real SetTemplateData()), so its decoupling instead relies on an invariant-result argument: with EnforceTenantFileScope=false throughout, the mutant's GetFile branch calls IgnoreQueryFilters() (no tenant predicate at all) while the fix's GetFileTenantScoped branch applies TenantCode == caller's tenant; for a file whose TenantCode already equals the caller's own tenant, an unfiltered query and a tenant-filtered query both return that same row -- the mutation changes WHICH query filter runs, not whether a same-tenant row is found, so this specific test's outcome (1 parsed row, 0 errors) is provably equal under both the fixed and mutated code. Included as a second, stronger check that the patch's declared blast radius (only the cross-tenant case) actually holds, on top of test (1)'s simpler complete-non-reachability argument.
